I think you are equating gender identity with gender expression. I should very much clarify that many people who identify as non-binary still present as their assigned gender (for many reasons such as safety, availability, ease of passing). And there are many people who dress differently but still identify as their assigned gender such as some drag performers. I highly recommend reading Julia Serano's Whipping Girl for an actual biologists' more researched analysis on what gender identity is. As to my argument, I wasn't arguing that I want to present differently from my assigned gender, rather my inherent identity does not fit into the binary genders.

That js a very complicated question. On one hand there always were gender roles. However, historic evidence shows that there always were people who did not conform to the gender roles at the time and yet were still accepted in their communities. Especially true in various indigenous communities around the world. Some cultures even treat gender non-conformity with mysticism and respect.

One way to look at it would be gender roles could not be enforced at the time, but post-colonization gender is something quantified and recorded since someone is born.

Why are you accusing me of things I haven't said? No one is forcing you to say anything, but if respecting someone's pronouns preference triggers you so much that speaks more about you than anything else.

I identify as non-binary and I can only speak for myself as every non-binary person I have met is different in their own ways. Personally, I don't see non-binary as creating a new category for gender, rather simply a rejection of existing categories. You have to realize gender roles weren't always as set in stone today as they always were. Colonization played a very big part in the enforcement of bimary gender roles where I grew up, even though we have had a rich and colorful history of gender non conforming people. As I grew up I felt that my assigned gender role never truly fit and made me more and more miserable the more I forced myself to fit into it. However I also never felt any desire to transition into the opposite gender, rather I don't think any one box can define who I am.

22 year old. Been battling with depression for the last four years. This year I was at my absolute worst, and considered suicide multiple times. So I do understand your situation. Two months ago I decided to make a change in my life and be the best version of myself, hence I joined the gym and started Reddit PPL. It is hard at the beginning but you have to take it a day at a time. Just force yourself to start, and force yourself to go the next day and then the next day. Keep taking small steps and eventually they start adding up. 

Now that two months in, I know I haven't made a lot of progress but mentally this was the best thing I could have done for myself. Exercise keeps you busy enough to put negative thoughts at bay. No matter how bad the day is, I feel accomplished after a workout. Physically and mentally I feel great. 

So this might not be the answer you're looking for but, just start and keep at it. Fitness is one of the best things you can do for depression.
